briefing_md:
Benign aggregate credit metrics mask a regime shift to higher-for-longer rates and sharply bifurcated risk pricing in the belly of structured and private credit.

The ensemble recession read remains quiet — NY Fed probit at the 8th percentile of the last 5y, EBP probit at the 6.8th, the ensemble at 14.7% and the 30th percentile — and the near-term forward spread has flipped firmly positive (83rd percentile). But the composition has changed: the move is being driven by the long end, with DGS10 at 4.96% (97.7th percentile) and 2s up 47 bps in three months, as the market reprices Warsh's Fed toward quarterly hikes and strips out the 2025 insurance cuts. T10Y3M steepening to 0.78 is a hawkish bear steepener, not a growth-friendly one. OFR FSI at the 30th percentile and EBP at -0.39 (6.8th percentile) confirm that systemic plumbing is still loose — this is a rates story, not yet a credit event.

Beneath the aggregate, credit dispersion is the real signal. BB data-center HY has widened ~136 bps since mid-September and trades through single-B, with intra-sector pricing from 222 to 848 bps — classic idiosyncratic repricing around 2030-31 refi walls and SPV structural risk. Getty's prepack adds to the AI-displacement bankruptcy tape. Direct lending volumes down 66% YoY and spreads compressed into a 490-530 bps band indicate the bank-loan market is winning the refi war and the private-credit countercyclical thesis is being tested in real time.

Consumer credit is mixed and worth flagging. Card 90+ DQ at 2.85% (33rd percentile) and card NCOs down 27 bps are reassuring, but single-family mortgage delinquency ticked up to 1.86% — the 77.8th percentile — against a 10y at 4.96% that keeps affordability punishing. This is the first consumer tape line pointing the wrong way.

Structured finance primary is sending a warning in the mezz. The "other"-segment mezzanine ABS print widened 60 bps vs. the prior deal, a 2.2σ move, while prime auto senior/mezz held firm (prime auto mezz actually tightened 26 bps). EDGAR filings skew heavily to mortgage (74) and royalty (65), with data-center ABS filings (16) continuing to build — the same sector seeing the HY repricing. CLO issuance (Obra's fifth, $2B+ cumulative) and the $5.5B LSEG/Octus and Tradeweb/Trumid credit-infra M&A tell you capital is still arriving, just more selectively.

watch_items.title: 10y yield breach of 5.00%
watch_items.why: DGS10 at 4.96% (97.7th percentile 5y) with a bear-steepening Fed repricing in progress; a decisive break would ratchet mortgage and leveraged-borrower stress.

watch_items.title: Single-family mortgage delinquency trajectory
watch_items.why: DRSFRMACBS at 1.86% is already at the 77.8th percentile and rose 7 bps in 3 months — the one consumer line diverging from the benign tape.

watch_items.title: BB data-center HY and 2030-31 refi wall
watch_items.why: 136 bps of widening since mid-September and 222-848 bps intra-sector dispersion signal idiosyncratic project-finance stress that could spill into related ABS filings.

watch_items.title: Mezzanine ABS repricing in 'other' segment
watch_items.why: Latest mezz print 2.2σ wider vs. prior deal while senior held — classic early sign of capital-stack discrimination before broader primary stress.

watch_items.title: Direct lending Q4 volume and spread band
watch_items.why: Q3 volume down 66% YoY with spreads compressed to 490-530 bps; another weak print would confirm structural loss of share to bank loans.

watch_items.title: EBP drift off -0.39
watch_items.why: At the 6.8th percentile, EBP is pinned low; any sustained lift above -0.20 would be the first aggregate credit confirmation of the idiosyncratic stress already visible in HY data center.

watch_items.title: Fed communication and 1y OIS path
watch_items.why: Warsh credibility question is the live macro variable; a repricing toward more than one hike per quarter would push the long end through 5% and tighten financial conditions non-linearly.

news_digests_recent.summary:
The single most dominant signal across markets is the Federal Reserve's posture shift: policymakers are now expected to revert to quarterly rate hikes after September's first increase since 2023, removing the 2025 "insurance cuts" that had been priced in. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's communication credibility is under scrutiny, with investors demanding clarity on the reaction function rather than further ambiguity. Financial conditions, not the rate level itself, are the variable to watch as 10-year yields move in lockstep with 1-year fed funds expectations, tightening the screws on rate-sensitive borrowers.

In credit, the most acute dislocation sits in BB-rated high-yield data center bonds, which have widened roughly 136 bps since mid-September and now trade approximately 150 bps wide of the single-B index — a pricing anomaly driven by project-finance SPV structures carrying construction, single-tenant concentration, and 2030-31 refinancing risk. Intra-sector dispersion is extreme: TeraWulf's Google-backstopped deal prices at 222 bps while Zenith Arc clears at 848 bps. Separately, junk borrowers broadly face a $2 trillion supply wall that lets investors be selective, pushing costs higher for the weakest names. Getty Images filed prepackaged Chapter 11 in Delaware on October 21, with equity and warrant holders contesting the prepack characterization amid AI-driven competitive pressure.

Direct lending had its worst quarter in three years, with Q3 2024 volume collapsing to $38.9 billion — down 66% year-over-year in September alone to $10.4 billion — as borrowers refinanced into bank loans at a 2.5-to-1 ratio. Spreads across size cohorts have compressed to a tight 490-530 bps band as larger managers crowd into sub-$20 million EBITDA deals, effectively breaking down the asset class's countercyclical pitch to LPs.

In structured finance, Obra Capital closed its fifth CLO at $403.6 million, pushing total issuance above $2 billion. Home equity investments are attracting renewed attention from Splitero's Michael Gifford, who argues that securitization demand could lower HEI pricing over time as elevated mortgage rates sustain origination volumes, though regulatory uncertainty remains an overhang. On the fintech infrastructure side, LSEG agreed to acquire credit intelligence provider Octus for $3.535 billion while Tradeweb struck a $1.97 billion deal for Trumid, together representing $5.5 billion in credit market infrastructure consolidation. Global fintech funding fell 21% year-over-year to $10.6 billion in Q3.
